project_overview: This Vue.js application appears to manage exam-related processes, including form submissions, results display, and user interactions with course recommendations. The application architecture leverages Vue components for UI elements, with a routing system to navigate between different sections. The dependency graph suggests a focus on user experience and data presentation, primarily driven by the Examination and User Engagement services.  The project uses multiple Vue components to represent various pages and processes related to student exams and course selections.

layers.description: Responsible for rendering the user interface and handling user interactions.
Contains the core application logic and services.

macro_trends.title: High-Level View Dependency Risk
macro_trends.description: Multiple Vue components (e.g., ApplicationServices, Transactions) are heavily reliant on routing and are directly linked to lower-level components, creating potential fragility and hard-to-maintain codebases. Centralized logic within the 'ApplicationServices' Vue component represents a potential 'God File' risk.

key_workflows.name: Exam Submission & Result Processing
key_workflows.description: This workflow involves user interactions through 'ExamFormSubmission.vue', data routing to 'SelectedApplicationService.vue' and 'Transactions.vue' for processing, and ultimately displaying results in 'ResultPage.vue' and 'viewMarksheet.vue'.  The components interrelate significantly, highlighting the core business logic.
